title: Đây là thị thực của tôi
pronunciation: Day la thi thuc cua toi
summary: Say "Here is my visa" with Đây là thị thực của tôi, then use the notes below to adjust tone and next steps.

sections.title: At a glance
sections.body: Use this when you are handing over a printed visa, e-visa, phone screenshot, or document folder. It tells staff exactly what the document is and that it belongs to you.

sections.title: Break it down
sections.body: Use this when you are showing a document or item. The phrase points to it, names it, then marks it as yours.

sections.title: The standard way
sections.body: Đây là thị thực của tôi is clear and formal enough for document checks. It works best while the visa is already visible in your hand or on your phone.

phrases.vietnamese: Đây là thị thực của tôi
phrases.pronunciation: Day la thi thuc cua toi

sections.title: Why it matters
sections.body: Airport phrases help staff route you to the next counter or service without a long explanation. For "Here is my visa", the useful move is naming the concrete item or problem first so staff can choose the next action. Show the document, photo, room number, receipt, or screen connected to the problem.

sections.title: Traveler insight
sections.body: In Airport Border Arrival, locals often answer with a request to see the item, a direction to another desk, or a practical next step rather than a long explanation. That makes Đây là thị thực của tôi strongest when you say it once, pause, and let the other person show the next step. Show the document, symptom, location, or item connected to the need so helpers can act faster.

sections.title: When to use it
sections.body: Use it at immigration, airline check-in, visa-on-arrival counters, or any desk where staff ask for visa proof.

sections.title: Good to know
sections.body: If the visa is on your phone, make sure the screen is bright and unlocked before you start. Staff may need the passport and visa together.

sections.title: Local tip
sections.body: Keep the passport open nearby. The fastest handoff is usually passport plus visa, not a long explanation.
